source.text: וַיִּגַּע֙ הַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י וּבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בֶּעָרִ֑יםסוַיֵּאָסְפ֥וּ הָעָ֛ם כְּאִ֥ישׁ אֶחָ֖ד אֶל־יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And arrived the month the seventh, and [the] sons of Israel [were] in the cities; and gathered the people as man one to Jerusalem.

en.L: And the seventh month came, and the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel were in the cities, and the people gathered as one man to Jerusalem.
en.B: When the seventh month came and the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} were settled in their towns, the people gathered in Jerusalem as one.
en.R: In the seventh month, when the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} had settled in their towns, all the people came together in Jerusalem, united.

es.L: Y llegó el mes séptimo, y los hijos de Israel [estaban] en las ciudades, y el pueblo se reunió como un solo hombre en Jerusalén.
es.B: Cuando llegó el mes séptimo y los israelitas ya estaban establecidos en sus ciudades, el pueblo se reunió en Jerusalén como un solo pueblo.
es.R: En el mes séptimo, cuando los israelitas ya se habían establecido en sus ciudades, todo el pueblo se reunió en Jerusalén, unido.

sw.L: Na mwezi wa saba ulipofika, nao wana wa Israeli [walikuwa] katika miji, watu wakakusanyika kama mtu mmoja huko Yerusalemu.
sw.B: Mwezi wa saba ulipofika, na Waisraeli walipokuwa wamekaa katika miji yao, watu walikusanyika Yerusalemu kama mtu mmoja.
sw.R: Katika mwezi wa saba, Waisraeli walipokuwa wamekwisha kukaa katika miji yao, watu wote walikusanyika Yerusalemu wakiwa na nia moja.

decisions.choice: the seventh month: the month of the autumn festivals
decisions.reason: The seventh month of Israel's year (later called Tishri) fell in September and October. It held the day of trumpet blasts on its first day, the Day of Atonement on the tenth and the Festival of Booths from the fifteenth (Leviticus 23:23-36). The year is not given; the account follows straight on from the return in chapter 2, so it is most naturally the first autumn after the exiles came home.

decisions.choice: as one man: all together, with one mind
decisions.reason: The phrase describes a whole people acting together without exception (Judges 20:1, 8, 11; Nehemiah 8:1). It says the gathering was complete and willing, not that the people were literally one.

decisions.choice: settled in their towns
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only that they were "in the cities"; Balanced and Readable say what that means after 2:70, where the returned exiles settled in their own towns. "Towns" suits the small settlements of Judah at that time; Literal keeps "cities".

decisions.choice: as one (Balanced); united (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture "as one man"; Balanced and Readable give its sense without the male image.

decisions.choice: "los hijos de Israel" (L); "los israelitas" (B, R); "como un solo hombre" (L); "como un solo pueblo" (B); "unido" (R)
decisions.reason: As in the published Spanish of Chronicles, "los israelitas" takes in men and women and needs no gender setting; Literal keeps the picture of one man, and Balanced and Readable give its sense, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "wana wa Israeli" (L), "Waisraeli" (B, R), with no gender span
decisions.reason: Swahili "wana" and "Waisraeli" both include women, so the English setting has nothing to change in Swahili, as in the earlier books.

decisions.choice: "kama mtu mmoja" kept at Balanced; Readable "wakiwa na nia moja"
decisions.reason: Swahili "mtu" is a person, not a man, so the picture carries no male image and Balanced can keep it.

source.text: וַיָּקָם֩ יֵשׁ֨וּעַ בֶּן־יֽוֹצָדָ֜ק וְאֶחָ֣יו הַכֹּהֲנִ֗ים וּזְרֻבָּבֶ֤ל בֶּן־שְׁאַלְתִּיאֵל֙ וְאֶחָ֔יו וַיִּבְנ֕וּ אֶת־מִזְבַּ֖ח אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לְהַעֲל֤וֹת עָלָיו֙ עֹל֔וֹת כַּכָּת֕וּב בְּתוֹרַ֖ת מֹשֶׁ֥ה אִישׁ־הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And arose Jeshua son of Jozadak and his brothers the priests, and Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and his brothers, and they built [the] altar of [the] God of Israel to offer up on it burnt offerings, as [is] written in [the] law of Moses, [the] man of God.

en.L: And Jeshua the son of Jozadak arose, and his brothers the priests, and Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel and his brothers, and they built the altar of the God of Israel, to offer up burnt offerings on it, as it is written in the law of Moses the man of God.
en.B: Then Jeshua son of Jozadak and his fellow priests, together with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and his relatives, set to work and built the altar of the God of Israel, so that they could offer burnt offerings on it as it is written in the law of Moses, the man of God.
en.R: Jeshua son of Jozadak and the other priests, along with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and his relatives, started the work. They built the altar of the God of Israel so they could offer burnt offerings on it, as it is written in the law of Moses, the man of God.

es.L: Y se levantó Jesúa hijo de Josadac, y sus hermanos los sacerdotes, y Zorobabel hijo de Salatiel y sus hermanos, y edificaron el altar del Dios de Israel, para ofrecer sobre él holocaustos, como está escrito en la ley de Moisés, hombre de Dios.
es.B: Entonces Jesúa hijo de Josadac y sus compañeros sacerdotes, junto con Zorobabel hijo de Salatiel y sus parientes, se pusieron a trabajar y edificaron el altar del Dios de Israel, para ofrecer sobre él holocaustos, como está escrito en la ley de Moisés, el hombre de Dios.
es.R: Jesúa hijo de Josadac y los demás sacerdotes, junto con Zorobabel hijo de Salatiel y sus parientes, comenzaron la obra. Construyeron el altar del Dios de Israel para poder ofrecer en él holocaustos, como está escrito en la ley de Moisés, el hombre de Dios.

sw.L: Ndipo Yeshua mwana wa Yosadaki akainuka, na ndugu zake makuhani, na Zerubabeli mwana wa Shealtieli na ndugu zake, wakaijenga madhabahu ya Mungu wa Israeli, ili kutoa sadaka za kuteketezwa juu yake, kama ilivyoandikwa katika sheria ya Musa mtu wa Mungu.
sw.B: Ndipo Yeshua mwana wa Yosadaki pamoja na makuhani wenzake, na Zerubabeli mwana wa Shealtieli pamoja na jamaa zake, walianza kazi, wakaijenga madhabahu ya Mungu wa Israeli, ili watoe sadaka za kuteketezwa juu yake kama ilivyoandikwa katika sheria ya Musa, mtu wa Mungu.
sw.R: Yeshua mwana wa Yosadaki na makuhani wengine, pamoja na Zerubabeli mwana wa Shealtieli na jamaa zake, walianza kazi. Waliijenga madhabahu ya Mungu wa Israeli ili watoe sadaka za kuteketezwa juu yake, kama ilivyoandikwa katika sheria ya Musa, mtu wa Mungu.

decisions.choice: Jeshua the priest and Zerubbabel: the two leaders of the return
decisions.reason: Jeshua son of Jozadak is the high priest, called Joshua in Haggai 1:1 and Zechariah 3:1; his father Jozadak was taken into exile by Nebuchadnezzar (1 Chronicles 5:41). Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel is of the royal line of David, a grandson of King Jehoiachin (1 Chronicles 3:17-19, which names his father as Pedaiah, Shealtiel's brother; Ezra, Nehemiah and Haggai always call him son of Shealtiel). Here the priest is named first because the work is the altar.

decisions.choice: arose: set to work
decisions.reason: The verb "arose" before another action marks a start, not a change of posture: they got up and did it (compare Nehemiah 2:18, "Let us arise and build").

decisions.choice: his brothers: his fellow priests; his kinsmen
decisions.reason: "Brothers" is used of members of the same group or family. With Jeshua it means the other priests; with Zerubbabel it means his relatives or the leading men of his clan.

decisions.choice: as written in the law of Moses: the burnt offerings the law commands
decisions.reason: The law commands burnt offerings on the altar every morning and evening and at the festivals (Exodus 29:38-42; Numbers 28-29). Moses is called "the man of God" also in Deuteronomy 33:1 and Psalm 90:1. The returned exiles restore worship by the written law before anything else.

decisions.choice: his fellow priests (Balanced), the other priests (Readable); his relatives
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who the "brothers" are, as meaning decision m3 explains; Literal keeps "brothers".

decisions.choice: "Jesúa hijo de Josadac", "Zorobabel hijo de Salatiel"
decisions.reason: Shealtiel as the published Spanish of Matthew 1:12 and 1 Chronicles 3:17 has him; Jozadak spelled as Jehozadak is in Spanish (Josadac).

decisions.choice: "sus compañeros sacerdotes" (B); "los demás sacerdotes" (R); "sus parientes" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who the "brothers" are (m3), as the English does; Literal keeps "hermanos".

decisions.choice: "Yosadaki", the short form, as the terms note
decisions.reason: Ezra spells the name short; 1 Chronicles 5:40-41 keeps the long "Yehosadaki" where the Hebrew has it.

source.text: וַיָּכִ֤ינוּ הַמִּזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ עַל־מְכ֣וֹנֹתָ֔יו כִּ֚י בְּאֵימָ֣ה עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם מֵעַמֵּ֖י הָאֲרָצ֑וֹת וַיַּעֲל֨וּעָלָ֤יו עֹלוֹת֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה עֹל֖וֹת לַבֹּ֥קֶר וְלָעָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And they set the altar on its foundations, for in terror [was] on them from [the] peoples of the lands; and they offered up on it burnt offerings to YHWH, burnt offerings for the morning and for the evening.

en.L: And they set up the altar on its foundations, for terror was on them because of the peoples of the lands; and they offered up burnt offerings on it to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, burnt offerings for the morning and for the evening.
en.B: They set the altar on its old foundations, because they were afraid of the peoples of the lands, and they offered burnt offerings on it to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the morning and evening burnt offerings.
en.R: They set up the altar where it had stood before, because they were afraid of the people living in the land. Then they offered burnt offerings on it to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} every morning and every evening.

es.L: Y asentaron el altar sobre sus bases, porque [había] terror sobre ellos a causa de los pueblos de las tierras; y ofrecieron sobre él holocaustos {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, holocaustos por la mañana y por la tarde.
es.B: Asentaron el altar sobre sus antiguas bases, porque tenían miedo de los pueblos de las tierras, y ofrecieron sobre él holocaustos {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, los holocaustos de la mañana y de la tarde.
es.R: Levantaron el altar en el mismo lugar donde había estado antes, porque tenían miedo de la gente que vivía en el país. Luego ofrecieron en él holocaustos {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} cada mañana y cada tarde.

sw.L: Wakaisimamisha madhabahu juu ya misingi yake, kwa maana hofu ilikuwa juu yao kwa sababu ya mataifa ya nchi; wakamtolea {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} sadaka za kuteketezwa juu yake, sadaka za kuteketezwa za asubuhi na za jioni.
sw.B: Waliisimamisha madhabahu juu ya misingi yake ya zamani, kwa sababu waliyaogopa mataifa ya nchi zile, wakamtolea {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} sadaka za kuteketezwa juu yake, sadaka za kuteketezwa za asubuhi na jioni.
sw.R: Waliisimamisha madhabahu mahali ilipokuwa hapo awali, kwa sababu waliwaogopa watu walioishi katika nchi ile. Kisha wakamtolea {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} sadaka za kuteketezwa juu yake kila asubuhi na kila jioni.

decisions.choice: on its foundations: on the place where the old altar had stood
decisions.reason: The word means a base or fixed place. They did not choose a new site but set the altar where the altar of Solomon's temple had been, as the law ties worship to the place the LORD chose (Deuteronomy 12:5-6).

decisions.choice: because they were afraid: fear was a reason for building the altar
decisions.reason: The joining word usually gives a reason: in danger, they turned first to the LORD's protection by restoring his worship. It can also be read as "even though": they built it in spite of their fear. The Hebrew allows both, and the second is close in effect, but "because" is the plainer sense.

decisions.choice: the peoples of the lands: the other peoples living in and around Judah
decisions.reason: The phrase means the populations who were not among the returned exiles: people settled in the north by the Assyrian kings (4:2, 10) and the neighboring peoples of the region. In Ezra and Nehemiah it marks those outside the community of the return, and they soon oppose the building (4:4). The plural "lands" points to more than one group.

decisions.choice: burnt offerings morning and evening: the daily offering
decisions.reason: The law commands a lamb as a burnt offering every morning and every evening (Exodus 29:38-42; Numbers 28:3-8). Restoring it restored the daily rhythm of Israel's worship.

decisions.choice: on its old foundations (Balanced); where it had stood before (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that the altar went back on its former site; Literal keeps "on its foundations".

decisions.choice: the people living in the land
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly who these are, as the Ezra and Nehemiah term list sets out; Literal and Balanced keep "the peoples of the lands".

decisions.choice: "la gente que vivía en el país" (R); "los pueblos de las tierras" (L, B)
decisions.reason: The terms note's wording for the peoples of the lands: Literal and Balanced keep the phrase, Readable says who they are, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "mataifa ya nchi" (L), "mataifa ya nchi zile" (B), "watu walioishi katika nchi ile" (R)
decisions.reason: Book-wide for the peoples of the land(s): the plural "mataifa" keeps the several groups apart from the returned exiles; Readable says who they were, as the English Readable.

source.text: וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֛וּ אֶת־חַ֥ג הַסֻּכּ֖וֹת כַּכָּת֑וּב וְעֹלַ֨ת י֤וֹם בְּיוֹם֙ בְּמִסְפָּ֔ר כְּמִשְׁפַּ֖ט דְּבַר־י֥וֹם בְּיוֹמֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they kept the festival of the booths as [is] written, and burnt offering of day in day by number according to [the] ordinance, [the] matter of [the] day in its day.

en.L: And they kept the Festival of Booths as it is written, and [offered] the burnt offering day by day in number according to the ordinance, the requirement of each day on its day.
en.B: They kept the Festival of Booths as it is written, and offered the daily burnt offerings, in the number the ordinance required for each day.
en.R: They celebrated the Festival of Booths as the law says. Each day they offered the number of burnt offerings that the law required for that day.

es.L: Y celebraron la fiesta de las Enramadas, como está escrito, y [ofrecieron] holocaustos día tras día en número conforme a lo establecido, lo de cada día en su día.
es.B: Celebraron la fiesta de las Enramadas, como está escrito, y ofrecieron los holocaustos diarios, en el número que lo establecido pedía para cada día.
es.R: Celebraron la fiesta de las Enramadas, como dice la ley. Cada día ofrecieron el número de holocaustos que la ley mandaba para ese día.

sw.L: Wakaishika Sikukuu ya Vibanda kama ilivyoandikwa, na [wakatoa] sadaka ya kuteketezwa siku kwa siku kwa hesabu sawasawa na agizo, jambo la kila siku katika siku yake.
sw.B: Waliishika Sikukuu ya Vibanda kama ilivyoandikwa, wakatoa sadaka za kuteketezwa za kila siku, kwa hesabu ambayo agizo liliitaka kwa kila siku.
sw.R: Waliisherehekea Sikukuu ya Vibanda kama sheria inavyosema. Kila siku walitoa idadi ya sadaka za kuteketezwa ambayo sheria iliagiza kwa siku hiyo.

decisions.choice: the Festival of Booths: the autumn harvest festival
decisions.reason: The festival ran for seven days from the fifteenth of the seventh month, with an eighth day of assembly. The people lived in shelters made of branches to remember how Israel lived when the LORD brought them out of Egypt (Leviticus 23:33-43; Deuteronomy 16:13-15).

decisions.choice: by number: the set number of animals for each day
decisions.reason: The law fixes a different number of bulls, rams and lambs for each day of the festival, from thirteen bulls on the first day down to seven on the seventh (Numbers 29:12-38). "As it is written" means they followed that list.

decisions.choice: the matter of a day in its day: what each day required
decisions.reason: The phrase is a fixed expression for a daily portion or duty (Exodus 5:13; 1 Kings 8:59; Nehemiah 11:23).

decisions.choice: [offered]
decisions.reason: The Hebrew lists the burnt offering without a verb, carrying on from "kept"; Literal supplies the verb in brackets, and Balanced and Readable add it plainly.

decisions.choice: "la fiesta de las Enramadas"
decisions.reason: The name of the Festival of Booths in the published Spanish of 2 Chronicles 8:13.

source.text: וְאַחֲרֵי כֵ֞ןעֹלַ֤ת תָּמִיד֙ וְלֶ֣חֳדָשִׁ֔ים וּלְכָל־מוֹעֲדֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה הַמְקֻדָּשִׁ֑ים וּלְכֹ֛ל מִתְנַדֵּ֥ב נְדָבָ֖ה לַיהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And after so, [the] burnt offering of continuity, and for the new moons and for all [the] appointed times of YHWH that were consecrated, and for every one freely offering a freewill offering to YHWH.

en.L: And after that, the continual burnt offering, and [the offerings] for the new moons and for all the appointed feasts of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that were consecrated, and for everyone who freely offered a freewill offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: After that they offered the regular burnt offering, the offerings for the new moons and for all the appointed festivals of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that had been made holy, and the offerings of everyone who brought a freewill offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: After this they offered the regular daily burnt offerings, and the offerings for the start of each month and for all the holy festivals of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They also offered the gifts that people chose to give to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Y después de esto, el holocausto continuo, y [las ofrendas] de las lunas nuevas y de todas las fiestas señaladas {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} que estaban consagradas, y de todo el que ofrecía voluntariamente una ofrenda voluntaria {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}.
es.B: Después de eso ofrecieron el holocausto continuo, las ofrendas de las lunas nuevas y de todas las fiestas señaladas {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} que habían sido consagradas, y las ofrendas de todos los que traían una ofrenda voluntaria {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}.
es.R: Después de esto ofrecieron los holocaustos diarios y las ofrendas para el comienzo de cada mes y para todas las fiestas sagradas {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. También ofrecieron los regalos que la gente quería darle {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Na baada ya hayo, sadaka ya kuteketezwa ya daima, na [sadaka] za mwandamo wa mwezi, na za sikukuu zote za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} zilizowekwa wakfu, na za kila mtu aliyetoa kwa hiari sadaka ya hiari kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Baada ya hayo walitoa sadaka ya kuteketezwa ya daima, sadaka za mwandamo wa mwezi na za sikukuu zote za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} zilizowekwa wakfu, na sadaka za kila mtu aliyemletea {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} sadaka ya hiari.
sw.R: Baada ya hayo walitoa sadaka za kuteketezwa za kila siku, sadaka za mwanzo wa kila mwezi na za sikukuu zote takatifu za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Pia walitoa zawadi ambazo watu walichagua kumpa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

decisions.choice: the continual burnt offering: the regular daily offering
decisions.reason: "Continual" names the morning and evening offering made every day without a break (Exodus 29:42; Numbers 28:3-10), which the other offerings were added to.

decisions.choice: the new moons and appointed feasts: the monthly and yearly holy days
decisions.reason: The new moon began each month and had its own offerings (Numbers 28:11-15). The appointed feasts are the festivals of Leviticus 23, which the LORD set apart as holy occasions.

decisions.choice: a freewill offering: a gift given by choice, beyond what the law required
decisions.reason: The freewill offering was given out of a person's own willingness, not for a vow or a duty (Leviticus 7:16; Deuteronomy 16:10). The returned exiles had already given freely for the house of God (1:4; 2:68).

decisions.choice: they offered
decisions.reason: The Hebrew continues the list from verse 4 without a verb; Balanced and Readable supply "offered", and Literal brackets "[the offerings]".

decisions.choice: the start of each month; the gifts that people chose to give
decisions.reason: Readable explains "new moons" and "freewill offering" in plain words.

decisions.choice: "mwanzo wa kila mwezi" and "zawadi ambazo watu walichagua kumpa" (R)
alternatives: mwandamo wa mwezi; sadaka ya hiari
decisions.reason: Readable explains the new moons and the freewill offering in plain words, as the English Readable.

source.text: מִיּ֤וֹם אֶחָד֙ לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י הֵחֵ֕לּוּ לְהַעֲל֥וֹת עֹל֖וֹת לַיהוָ֑ה וְהֵיכַ֥ל יְהוָ֖ה לֹ֥א יֻסָּֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: From day one of the month the seventh they began to offer up burnt offerings to YHWH, and [the] temple of YHWH not was founded.

en.L: From the first day of the seventh month they began to offer up burnt offerings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, but the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was not [yet] founded.
en.B: From the first day of the seventh month they began to offer burnt offerings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, though the foundation of the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had not yet been laid.
en.R: They began to offer burnt offerings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on the first day of the seventh month, even though the foundation of the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had not been laid yet.

es.L: Desde el primer día del mes séptimo comenzaron a ofrecer holocaustos {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, pero el templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} no estaba [aún] cimentado.
es.B: Desde el primer día del mes séptimo comenzaron a ofrecer holocaustos {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, aunque todavía no se habían echado los cimientos del templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.R: Comenzaron a ofrecer holocaustos {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} el primer día del mes séptimo, aunque todavía no se habían puesto los cimientos del templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Tangu siku ya kwanza ya mwezi wa saba walianza kumtolea {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} sadaka za kuteketezwa, lakini hekalu la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} lilikuwa [bado] halijawekewa msingi.
sw.B: Tangu siku ya kwanza ya mwezi wa saba walianza kumtolea {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} sadaka za kuteketezwa, ingawa msingi wa hekalu la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ulikuwa bado haujawekwa.
sw.R: Walianza kumtolea {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} sadaka za kuteketezwa siku ya kwanza ya mwezi wa saba, ingawa msingi wa hekalu la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ulikuwa bado haujawekwa.

decisions.choice: the first day of the seventh month: a holy day of trumpet blasts
decisions.reason: The law makes the first day of the seventh month a day of rest and of trumpet blasts, with its own offerings (Leviticus 23:24-25; Numbers 29:1-6). So the offerings began on a festival day, two weeks before the Festival of Booths of verse 4.

decisions.choice: the temple was not founded: its foundation had not been laid
alternatives: the temple was not yet restored
decisions.reason: The word for "temple" names the main building of the LORD's house. The verb means to lay a foundation; the point is that worship at the altar started before any building work on the temple (verse 10).

decisions.choice: [yet] (Literal); not yet (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says simply "was not founded"; English needs "yet" to show that the founding came later (verse 10). Literal brackets it.

source.text: וַיִּ֨תְּנוּ־כֶ֔סֶף לַחֹצְבִ֖ים וְלֶחָרָשִׁ֑ים וּמַאֲכָ֨ל וּמִשְׁתֶּ֜ה וָשֶׁ֗מֶן לַצִּֽדֹנִים֙ וְלַצֹּרִ֔ים לְהָבִיא֩ עֲצֵ֨י אֲרָזִ֤ים מִן־הַלְּבָנוֹן֙ אֶל־יָ֣ם יָפ֔וֹא כְּרִשְׁי֛וֹן כּ֥וֹרֶשׁ מֶֽלֶךְ־פָּרַ֖ס עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And they gave silver to the stonecutters and to the craftsmen, and food and drink and oil to the Sidonians and to the Tyrians, to bring trees of cedars from the Lebanon to [the] sea [of] Joppa, according to [the] permission of Cyrus king of Persia to them.

en.L: And they gave silver to the stonecutters and to the craftsmen, and food and drink and oil to the Sidonians and to the Tyrians, to bring cedar wood from Lebanon to the sea at Joppa, according to the grant of Cyrus king of Persia to them.
en.B: They gave money to the stonecutters and the craftsmen, and food, drink and olive oil to the people of Sidon and Tyre, so that they would bring cedar logs from Lebanon by sea to Joppa, as Cyrus king of Persia had authorized them.
en.R: They paid money to the stoneworkers and the skilled workers. They gave food, drink and olive oil to the people of Sidon and Tyre to bring cedar logs from Lebanon by sea to the port of Joppa. King Cyrus of Persia had given them permission to do this.

es.L: Y dieron plata a los canteros y a los artesanos, y comida y bebida y aceite a los sidonios y a los tirios, para que trajeran madera de cedro del Líbano por mar a Jope, conforme al permiso que Ciro rey de Persia les había dado.
es.B: Dieron dinero a los canteros y a los artesanos, y comida, bebida y aceite de oliva a la gente de Sidón y de Tiro, para que trajeran troncos de cedro del Líbano por mar hasta Jope, como Ciro rey de Persia les había autorizado.
es.R: Pagaron dinero a los que trabajaban la piedra y a los artesanos. A la gente de Sidón y de Tiro le dieron comida, bebida y aceite de oliva para que trajeran troncos de cedro del Líbano por mar hasta el puerto de Jope. Ciro, rey de Persia, les había dado permiso para hacerlo.

sw.L: Wakawapa fedha wachonga mawe na mafundi, na chakula na kinywaji na mafuta Wasidoni na Watiro, ili walete miti ya mierezi kutoka Lebanoni mpaka bahari ya Yafa, sawasawa na ruhusa ya Koreshi mfalme wa Uajemi kwao.
sw.B: Waliwapa fedha wachonga mawe na mafundi, na chakula, kinywaji na mafuta ya zeituni watu wa Sidoni na Tiro, ili walete magogo ya mierezi kutoka Lebanoni kwa njia ya bahari mpaka Yafa, kama Koreshi mfalme wa Uajemi alivyokuwa amewaruhusu.
sw.R: Waliwalipa fedha mafundi wa mawe na mafundi stadi. Waliwapa watu wa Sidoni na Tiro chakula, kinywaji na mafuta ya zeituni ili walete magogo ya mierezi kutoka Lebanoni kwa njia ya bahari mpaka bandari ya Yafa. Koreshi mfalme wa Uajemi alikuwa amewapa ruhusa kufanya hivyo.

decisions.choice: cedar from Lebanon through Sidon and Tyre: as for Solomon's temple
decisions.reason: Solomon got cedar from Lebanon for the first temple from Hiram king of Tyre, paying in food and oil, and the logs were floated by sea to Joppa (1 Kings 5:15-25; 2 Chronicles 2:2-15, as the Hebrew text numbers them). The new building begins the same way.

decisions.choice: to the sea of Joppa: to the coast at Joppa, by sea
decisions.reason: Joppa (modern Jaffa) was the seaport nearest to Jerusalem. The timber came down the coast by sea from the Phoenician cities and then went overland to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: the grant of Cyrus: the permission Cyrus gave them
decisions.reason: The noun appears only here in the Hebrew Bible; from its root it means permission or authorization. It points back to Cyrus's decree allowing the house of God to be built (1:2-4; 6:3-5).

decisions.choice: stonecutters and craftsmen: the workers in stone and in wood
decisions.reason: The first word means those who cut and dress stone. The second is a general word for a skilled worker in wood, stone or metal; beside the stonecutters and the cedar it probably means mainly carpenters.

decisions.choice: money; olive oil
decisions.reason: The word for "silver" also means money, which is the point here; Literal keeps "silver". The oil of Israel's trade was olive oil.

decisions.choice: "dinero"; "aceite de oliva" (B, R); "plata", "aceite" (L)
decisions.reason: As the English: the word for silver here means money, and the oil is olive oil; Literal keeps the bare words. Joppa is "Jope" as in 2 Chronicles 2:15.

decisions.choice: "Yafa" for Joppa
decisions.reason: The Swahili New Testament's form (Acts 9:36), kept for the same port.

source.text: וּבַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשֵּׁנִ֗ית לְבוֹאָ֞ם אֶל־בֵּ֤ית הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ לִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם בַּחֹ֖דֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִ֑י הֵחֵ֡לּוּ זְרֻבָּבֶ֣ל בֶּן־שְׁ֠אַלְתִּיאֵל וְיֵשׁ֨וּעַ בֶּן־יֽוֹצָדָ֜ק וּשְׁאָ֥ר אֲחֵיהֶ֣ם׀הַכֹּהֲנִ֣ים וְהַלְוִיִּ֗ם וְכָל־הַבָּאִים֙ מֵהַשְּׁבִ֣י יְרֽוּשָׁלִַ֔ם וַיַּעֲמִ֣ידוּ אֶת־הַלְוִיִּ֗ם מִבֶּ֨ן עֶשְׂרִ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ וָמַ֔עְלָה לְנַצֵּ֖חַ עַל־מְלֶ֥אכֶת בֵּית־יְהוָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And in the year the second of their coming to [the] house of God to Jerusalem, in the month the second, began Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak and [the] rest of their brothers, the priests and the Levites, and all those coming from the captivity [to] Jerusalem; and they appointed the Levites from [a] son of twenty year[s] and upward to oversee over [the] work of [the] house of YHWH.

en.L: And in the second year of their coming to the house of God at Jerusalem, in the second month, Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel and Jeshua the son of Jozadak began, and the rest of their brothers, the priests and the Levites, and all who had come from the captivity to Jerusalem; and they appointed the Levites, from twenty years old and upward, to oversee the work of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: In the second month of the second year after they came to the house of God in Jerusalem, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak began the work, together with the rest of their people: the priests, the Levites and all who had come back to Jerusalem from captivity. They appointed the Levites who were twenty years old or more to oversee the work on the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: The work began in the second month of the second year after they arrived at the place of God's temple in Jerusalem. Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, Jeshua son of Jozadak and all the rest of the people started it: the priests, the Levites and everyone who had come back to Jerusalem from exile. They put the Levites who were twenty years old or older in charge of the work on the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Y en el segundo año de su llegada a la casa de Dios en Jerusalén, en el mes segundo, comenzaron Zorobabel hijo de Salatiel y Jesúa hijo de Josadac, y el resto de sus hermanos, los sacerdotes y los levitas, y todos los que habían venido del cautiverio a Jerusalén; y pusieron a los levitas de veinte años para arriba para dirigir la obra de la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.B: En el mes segundo del segundo año después de llegar a la casa de Dios en Jerusalén, Zorobabel hijo de Salatiel y Jesúa hijo de Josadac comenzaron la obra, junto con el resto de su pueblo: los sacerdotes, los levitas y todos los que habían vuelto del cautiverio a Jerusalén. Pusieron a los levitas de veinte años o más para dirigir la obra de la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.R: La obra comenzó en el mes segundo del segundo año después de que llegaron al lugar del templo de Dios en Jerusalén. Zorobabel hijo de Salatiel, Jesúa hijo de Josadac y todo el resto del pueblo la comenzaron: los sacerdotes, los levitas y todos los que habían vuelto del destierro a Jerusalén. Pusieron a cargo de la obra del templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} a los levitas de veinte años o más.

sw.L: Na katika mwaka wa pili wa kuja kwao kwenye nyumba ya Mungu huko Yerusalemu, katika mwezi wa pili, Zerubabeli mwana wa Shealtieli na Yeshua mwana wa Yosadaki wakaanza, na ndugu zao waliobaki, makuhani na Walawi, na wote waliokuja kutoka utumwani mpaka Yerusalemu; wakawaweka Walawi, tangu wenye umri wa miaka ishirini na zaidi, kusimamia kazi ya nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Katika mwezi wa pili wa mwaka wa pili tangu walipofika kwenye nyumba ya Mungu huko Yerusalemu, Zerubabeli mwana wa Shealtieli na Yeshua mwana wa Yosadaki walianza kazi, pamoja na watu wao wengine wote: makuhani, Walawi na wote waliorudi Yerusalemu kutoka utumwani. Waliwaweka Walawi wenye umri wa miaka ishirini na zaidi kusimamia kazi ya nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Kazi ilianza katika mwezi wa pili wa mwaka wa pili tangu walipofika mahali pa hekalu la Mungu huko Yerusalemu. Zerubabeli mwana wa Shealtieli, Yeshua mwana wa Yosadaki na watu wengine wote waliianza: makuhani, Walawi na kila mtu aliyerudi Yerusalemu kutoka uhamishoni. Waliwaweka Walawi wenye umri wa miaka ishirini au zaidi wasimamie kazi ya hekalu la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

decisions.choice: the second month of the second year: spring, about a year and a half after the return
decisions.reason: The second month fell in April and May. Solomon also began building the first temple in the second month (1 Kings 6:1; 2 Chronicles 3:2). The year is counted from the exiles' arrival, which followed Cyrus's decree in his first year (1:1).

decisions.choice: the house of God: its site, still in ruins
decisions.reason: No house of God was standing when they arrived; the phrase names the place where it had stood and was to be rebuilt (compare 2:68, "the house of the LORD which is in Jerusalem").

decisions.choice: Levites from twenty years old: the age David set
decisions.reason: The law of Moses set the Levites' service from thirty (Numbers 4:3) or twenty-five (Numbers 8:24). David lowered it to twenty when the work of the house grew (1 Chronicles 23:24, 27), and the returned community follows David's rule. There were few Levites among the returned exiles (2:40), which may also explain it.

decisions.choice: their brothers ... the captivity: the whole community of the return
decisions.reason: "Brothers" here means fellow members of the people, listed as the priests, the Levites and all the returned exiles. "The captivity" is the exile in Babylon.

decisions.choice: the rest of their people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "people" for "brothers", since the list that follows is the whole community, men and women; Literal keeps "brothers".

decisions.choice: the place of God's temple
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the house of God was not standing yet (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: "el resto de su pueblo" (B); "todo el resto del pueblo" (R); "el resto de sus hermanos" (L)
decisions.reason: The list that follows is the whole community, men and women, so Balanced and Readable say "pueblo" for "brothers", as the English does.

source.text: וַיַּעֲמֹ֣ד יֵשׁ֡וּעַ בָּנָ֣יו וְ֠אֶחָיו קַדְמִיאֵ֨ל וּבָנָ֤יו בְּנֵֽי־יְהוּדָה֙ כְּאֶחָ֔ד לְנַצֵּ֛חַ עַל־עֹשֵׂ֥ה הַמְּלָאכָ֖ה בְּבֵ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֑יםסבְּנֵי֙ חֵֽנָדָ֔ד בְּנֵיהֶ֥ם וַאֲחֵיהֶ֖ם הַלְוִיִּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And stood Jeshua, his sons and his brothers, Kadmiel and his sons, [the] sons of Judah, as one, to oversee over [the] doers of the work in [the] house of God; [the] sons of Henadad, their sons and their brothers, the Levites.

en.L: And Jeshua stood, his sons and his brothers, Kadmiel and his sons, the sons of Judah, as one, to oversee the doers of the work on the house of God; the sons of Henadad, their sons and their brothers, the Levites.
en.B: Jeshua with his sons and his relatives, and Kadmiel and his sons, the descendants of Judah, took their places together to oversee the workers on the house of God, with the descendants of Henadad and their sons and relatives, the Levites.
en.R: The Levite Jeshua with his sons and relatives, and Kadmiel and his sons, the descendants of Judah, joined together to direct the workers on God's temple. The family of Henadad, with their sons and relatives, who were also Levites, worked with them.

es.L: Y se presentó Jesúa, sus hijos y sus hermanos, Cadmiel y sus hijos, los hijos de Judá, como uno solo, para dirigir a los que hacían la obra en la casa de Dios; los hijos de Henadad, sus hijos y sus hermanos, los levitas.
es.B: Jesúa con sus hijos y sus parientes, y Cadmiel y sus hijos, los descendientes de Judá, ocuparon juntos sus puestos para dirigir a los obreros de la casa de Dios, junto con los descendientes de Henadad y sus hijos y parientes, los levitas.
es.R: El levita Jesúa con sus hijos y parientes, y Cadmiel y sus hijos, los descendientes de Judá, se unieron para dirigir a los obreros del templo de Dios. La familia de Henadad, con sus hijos y parientes, que también eran levitas, trabajó con ellos.

sw.L: Ndipo Yeshua akasimama, wanawe na ndugu zake, Kadmieli na wanawe, wana wa Yuda, kama mmoja, kuwasimamia wafanyao kazi katika nyumba ya Mungu; wana wa Henadadi, wana wao na ndugu zao, Walawi.
sw.B: Yeshua pamoja na wanawe na jamaa zake, na Kadmieli na wanawe, wazao wa Yuda, walichukua nafasi zao pamoja kuwasimamia wafanyakazi katika nyumba ya Mungu, pamoja na wazao wa Henadadi na wana wao na jamaa zao, Walawi.
sw.R: Mlawi Yeshua pamoja na wanawe na jamaa zake, na Kadmieli na wanawe, wazao wa Yuda, waliungana kuwaongoza wafanyakazi wa hekalu la Mungu. Jamaa ya Henadadi pamoja na wana wao na jamaa zao, ambao pia walikuwa Walawi, walifanya kazi pamoja nao.

decisions.choice: Jeshua, Kadmiel and Henadad: Levite families
decisions.reason: This Jeshua is not the high priest of verses 2 and 8. Jeshua and Kadmiel head a family of Levites in the list of returned exiles (2:40), and the families of Jeshua, Kadmiel and Henadad appear together among the Levites in Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:10; 12:8). The verse names the Levite overseers appointed in verse 8.

decisions.choice: the sons of Judah: perhaps the family of Hodaviah
decisions.reason: In 2:40 Jeshua and Kadmiel are "of the sons of Hodaviah", and a Levite family is hardly called the sons of Judah. Hodaviah and Judah are similar in Hebrew and may have been confused in copying; or Judah may be another name of the same family. The Hebrew text says "Judah", and that is kept.

decisions.choice: stood as one: took up their posts together
decisions.reason: "Stood" means took up a position or duty, and "as one" means all together, as in verse 1.

decisions.choice: The Levite Jeshua
decisions.reason: Readable adds "Levite" so that the reader does not take him for the high priest Jeshua of verse 8 (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: the descendants of Judah; the descendants of Henadad
decisions.reason: Balanced follows the Ezra term list for family names, "the descendants of".

decisions.choice: "El levita Jesúa" (R)
decisions.reason: Readable adds "levita" so that this Jesúa is not taken for the high priest of verse 8 (m1), as the English Readable does.

source.text: וְיִסְּד֥וּ הַבֹּנִ֖ים אֶת־הֵיכַ֣ל יְהוָ֑ה וַיַּעֲמִידוּ֩ הַכֹּהֲנִ֨ים מְלֻבָּשִׁ֜ים בַּחֲצֹֽצְר֗וֹת וְהַלְוִיִּ֤ם בְּנֵֽי־אָסָף֙ בַּֽמְצִלְתַּ֔יִם לְהַלֵּל֙ אֶת־יְהוָ֔ה עַל־יְדֵ֖י דָּוִ֥יד מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And founded the builders [the] temple of YHWH, and they stationed the priests clothed with trumpets, and the Levites, [the] sons of Asaph, with cymbals, to praise YHWH on [the] hands of David king of Israel.

en.L: And the builders laid the foundation of the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they stationed the priests, clothed [in their vestments], with trumpets, and the Levites, the sons of Asaph, with cymbals, to praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} according to the hands of David king of Israel.
en.B: When the builders laid the foundation of the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the priests in their vestments were stationed with trumpets, and the Levites, the descendants of Asaph, with cymbals, to praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as David king of Israel had directed.
en.R: When the builders laid the foundation of the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the priests stood in their priestly robes with trumpets, and the Levites from the family of Asaph stood with cymbals. They praised {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in the way that King David of Israel had set out long before.

es.L: Y los constructores echaron los cimientos del templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y pusieron a los sacerdotes, vestidos [con sus vestiduras], con trompetas, y a los levitas, hijos de Asaf, con címbalos, para alabar {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} conforme a las manos de David rey de Israel.
es.B: Cuando los constructores echaron los cimientos del templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, los sacerdotes con sus vestiduras se colocaron con trompetas, y los levitas, descendientes de Asaf, con címbalos, para alabar {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} como lo había dispuesto David rey de Israel.
es.R: Cuando los constructores pusieron los cimientos del templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, los sacerdotes se pusieron de pie con sus ropas sacerdotales y con trompetas, y los levitas de la familia de Asaf se pusieron de pie con címbalos. Alabaron {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} de la manera que el rey David de Israel había ordenado mucho tiempo antes.

sw.L: Na wajenzi wakauweka msingi wa hekalu la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nao wakawasimamisha makuhani, wamevaa [mavazi yao], wakiwa na tarumbeta, na Walawi, wana wa Asafu, wakiwa na matoazi, ili kumsifu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kwa mikono ya Daudi mfalme wa Israeli.
sw.B: Wajenzi walipouweka msingi wa hekalu la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, makuhani waliovaa mavazi yao walisimamishwa wakiwa na tarumbeta, na Walawi, wazao wa Asafu, wakiwa na matoazi, ili kumsifu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kama Daudi mfalme wa Israeli alivyoagiza.
sw.R: Wajenzi walipouweka msingi wa hekalu la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, makuhani walisimama wakiwa wamevaa mavazi yao ya kikuhani na kushika tarumbeta, na Walawi wa ukoo wa Asafu walisimama na matoazi. Walimsifu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kwa njia ambayo Daudi mfalme wa Israeli alikuwa ameipanga zamani.

decisions.choice: on the hands of David: as David had arranged
decisions.reason: "By the hands of" someone means under his direction or by his arrangement. David organized the Levite singers and musicians and the priests' trumpets for the worship of the LORD (1 Chronicles 16:4-6; 25:1; 2 Chronicles 29:25-27).

decisions.choice: priests with trumpets, the sons of Asaph with cymbals
decisions.reason: The law gives the trumpets to the priests (Numbers 10:8), and they blew them when the ark came to the first temple (2 Chronicles 5:12-13). Asaph was one of David's chief musicians (1 Chronicles 16:5), and his descendants were the temple singers among the returned exiles (2:41).

decisions.choice: clothed: wearing their priestly vestments
decisions.reason: The word means "dressed" or "clothed"; used of priests on duty it means in the garments the law prescribes for them (Exodus 28; 2 Chronicles 5:12).

decisions.choice: clothed [in their vestments] (Literal); in their vestments (Balanced); in their priestly robes (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has only "clothed"; English needs to say in what. Readable uses the plainer "robes".

decisions.choice: "vestidos [con sus vestiduras]" (L); "con sus vestiduras" (B); "con sus ropas sacerdotales" (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has only "clothed" (m3); the levels supply what, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "kama Daudi ... alivyoagiza" (B), "kwa njia ambayo Daudi ... alikuwa ameipanga" (R); Literal keeps "kwa mikono ya Daudi"
decisions.reason: "By the hands of" means by David's arrangement; a Swahili reader would take the literal phrase as David doing it himself.

source.text: וַֽ֠יַּעֲנוּ בְּהַלֵּ֨ל וּבְהוֹדֹ֤ת לַֽיהוָה֙ כִּ֣י ט֔וֹב כִּֽי־לְעוֹלָ֥ם חַסְדּ֖וֹ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְכָל־הָעָ֡ם הֵרִיעוּ֩ תְרוּעָ֨הגְדוֹלָ֤ה בְהַלֵּל֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה עַ֖ל הוּסַ֥ד בֵּית־יְהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And they answered with praising and with giving thanks to YHWH: for [he is] good, for to forever [is] his steadfast love over Israel. And all the people shouted a shout great with praising to YHWH because was founded [the] house of YHWH.

en.L: And they sang responsively, praising and giving thanks to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: "For [{{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is] good, for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} steadfast love toward Israel [is] forever." And all the people shouted with a great shout, praising {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, because the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was founded.
en.B: They sang in response to one another, praising and giving thanks to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: "He is good; {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithful love for Israel lasts forever." And all the people gave a great shout of praise to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, because the foundation of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had been laid.
en.R: They sang back and forth, praising and thanking {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: "He is good! His faithful love for Israel lasts forever." All the people shouted loudly and praised {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, because the foundation of the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had been laid.

es.L: Y cantaban alternándose, alabando y dando gracias {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}: «Porque [{{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es] bueno, porque {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} amor leal para con Israel [es] para siempre». Y todo el pueblo gritó con gran júbilo, alabando {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, porque se habían echado los cimientos de la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.B: Cantaban respondiéndose unos a otros, alabando y dando gracias {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}: «Él es bueno; {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} amor fiel por Israel dura para siempre». Y todo el pueblo lanzó un gran grito de alabanza {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, porque se habían echado los cimientos de la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.R: Cantaban por turnos, alabando y dando gracias {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}: «¡Él es bueno! Su amor fiel por Israel dura para siempre». Todo el pueblo gritaba con fuerza y alababa {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, porque ya se habían puesto los cimientos del templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Wakaimba kwa kupokezana, wakimsifu na kumshukuru {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}: "Kwa maana [{{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni] mwema, kwa maana upendo {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} usiokoma kwa Israeli [ni] wa milele." Na watu wote wakapiga kelele kwa sauti kuu, wakimsifu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwa sababu nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ilikuwa imewekewa msingi.
sw.B: Waliimba kwa kupokezana, wakimsifu na kumshukuru {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}: "Yeye ni mwema; upendo {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} usiokoma kwa Israeli unadumu milele." Watu wote wakapiga kelele kuu ya kumsifu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwa sababu msingi wa nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ulikuwa umewekwa.
sw.R: Waliimba kwa zamu, wakimsifu na kumshukuru {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}: "Yeye ni mwema! Upendo {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} usiokoma kwa Israeli unadumu milele." Watu wote wakapiga kelele kwa nguvu na kumsifu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwa sababu msingi wa hekalu la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ulikuwa umewekwa.

decisions.choice: answered: sang in response, one group answering another
decisions.reason: "Answer" is used of singing back and forth, one group calling and the other responding (Exodus 15:21; 1 Samuel 18:7). The priests and Levites of verse 10 sang the praise in turns.

decisions.choice: for he is good, for his steadfast love is forever: the temple refrain
decisions.reason: These are the words of the well-known song of thanks (Psalm 106:1; 107:1; 118:1; 136:1). They were sung when the ark was brought into Solomon's temple and when it was dedicated (2 Chronicles 5:13; 7:3). Here they are sung again at the start of the second temple, with "toward Israel" added.

decisions.choice: steadfast love: the LORD's loyal, covenant kindness
decisions.reason: The word means love that keeps faith with a bond or covenant: kindness that does not give up. Ezra uses it of God's favor shown through the Persian kings (7:28; 9:9).

decisions.choice: a great shout: a loud cry of joy and acclaim
decisions.reason: The word is the shout raised at a festival, a victory or a king's coming (1 Samuel 4:5; Psalm 47:6), here in praise as the work began.

decisions.choice: steadfast love (Literal); faithful love (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The Numbers to Ruth term list, which applies to Ezra, gives these words for this term.

decisions.choice: He is good; ... lasts forever
decisions.reason: The two "for" words introduce what is sung; Balanced and Readable leave them out and quote the words directly, while Literal keeps them.

decisions.choice: "porque [él es] bueno, porque su amor leal ... [es] para siempre" (L); "Él es bueno; su amor fiel ... dura para siempre" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The temple refrain in the published wording of Psalm 136:1, with "para con Israel" / "por Israel" added as the Hebrew adds it; "amor leal" (L) and "amor fiel" (B, R) for *ḥesed*, as the terms note sets them.

decisions.choice: the refrain in the wording of the Swahili Psalm 136:1 at each level, with "kwa Israeli" added; "upendo usiokoma" at every level
decisions.reason: Ezra 3:11 sings the temple refrain; keeping the published Psalm wording lets a reader hear it, and only what the Hebrew adds is added.

source.text: וְרַבִּ֡ים מֵהַכֹּהֲנִ֣ים וְהַלְוִיִּם֩ וְרָאשֵׁ֨י הָאָב֜וֹת הַזְּקֵנִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר רָא֜וּ אֶת־הַבַּ֤יִת הָֽרִאשׁוֹן֙ בְּיָסְד֔וֹ זֶ֤ה הַבַּ֨יִת֙ בְּעֵ֣ינֵיהֶ֔ם בֹּכִ֖ים בְּק֣וֹל גָּד֑וֹל וְרַבִּ֛ים בִּתְרוּעָ֥ה בְשִׂמְחָ֖ה לְהָרִ֥ים קֽוֹל׃

records.literal_gloss: And many of the priests and the Levites and [the] heads of the fathers, the old [men] who had seen the house the first, at its founding, this the house, in their eyes, [were] weeping with a voice great; and many [were] with shout in joy to lift [the] voice.

en.L: And many of the priests and the Levites and the heads of the fathers' [houses], the old men who had seen the first house, when this house was founded before their eyes, were weeping with a loud voice; and many [were] shouting with joy, lifting up [their] voice.
en.B: But many of the priests and Levites and heads of families, the old men who had seen the first temple, wept aloud when they saw the foundation of this temple laid, while many others shouted for joy.
en.R: Many of the older priests, Levites and family leaders had seen the first temple. When they saw the foundation of this temple being laid, they cried loudly. But many others shouted with joy.

es.L: Y muchos de los sacerdotes y de los levitas y de los jefes de las [casas] paternas, los ancianos que habían visto la primera casa, cuando se echaron los cimientos de esta casa ante sus ojos, lloraban en alta voz; y muchos [daban] gritos de alegría, alzando [la] voz.
es.B: Pero muchos de los sacerdotes, los levitas y los jefes de familia, los ancianos que habían visto el primer templo, lloraban en voz alta al ver echar los cimientos de este templo, mientras muchos otros gritaban de alegría.
es.R: Muchos de los sacerdotes, levitas y jefes de familia de más edad habían visto el primer templo. Cuando vieron que se ponían los cimientos de este templo, lloraron en voz alta. Pero muchos otros gritaban de alegría.

sw.L: Na wengi wa makuhani na Walawi na wakuu wa [nyumba za] baba, wazee waliokuwa wameiona nyumba ya kwanza, nyumba hii ilipowekewa msingi mbele ya macho yao, walikuwa wakilia kwa sauti kuu; na wengi [walikuwa] wakipiga kelele kwa furaha, wakipaza sauti.
sw.B: Lakini wengi wa makuhani na Walawi na wakuu wa jamaa, wazee waliokuwa wameliona hekalu la kwanza, walilia kwa sauti kubwa walipoona msingi wa hekalu hili ukiwekwa, huku wengine wengi wakipiga kelele kwa furaha.
sw.R: Wengi wa makuhani, Walawi na viongozi wa jamaa waliokuwa wazee walikuwa wameliona hekalu la kwanza. Walipoona msingi wa hekalu hili ukiwekwa, walilia kwa sauti kubwa. Lakini wengine wengi walipiga kelele kwa furaha.

decisions.choice: the first house: Solomon's temple
decisions.reason: The first temple was burned by the Babylonians in 586 BC (2 Kings 25:9). This foundation was laid some fifty years later, so only the old could remember it.

decisions.choice: at its founding, this house, in their eyes: when this house was founded before their eyes
alternatives: who had seen the first house standing on its foundation
decisions.reason: The words are short and loosely joined. They are best read as one phrase: when the foundation of this house was laid in front of them. Another reading takes "at its founding" with the first house, "who had seen the first house on its foundation", and "this house in their eyes" as how the new one looked to them (compare Haggai 2:3). The sense, old men comparing the new with the old, is the same.

decisions.choice: weeping with a loud voice: the text does not say why
decisions.reason: Their weeping is set against the others' shouts of joy. Haggai 2:3 says that to those who had seen the former glory the new house looked like nothing; grief for what was lost is the natural reading, but the text itself does not give a reason.

decisions.choice: heads of the fathers: heads of families
decisions.reason: "The fathers" is short for "the fathers' houses", the extended families that made up the clans (2:59, 68).

decisions.choice: temple
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "temple" for "house" here, where the first and second buildings are compared, so that the reader is not left to work out which house is meant; Literal keeps "house".

decisions.choice: "templo" (B, R); "casa" (L)
decisions.reason: Where the first and second buildings are compared, Balanced and Readable say "templo", as the English does; Literal keeps "casa".

source.text: וְאֵ֣ין הָעָ֗ם מַכִּירִים֙ ק֚וֹל תְּרוּעַ֣ת הַשִּׂמְחָ֔ה לְק֖וֹל בְּכִ֣י הָעָ֑ם כִּ֣י הָעָ֗ם מְרִיעִים֙ תְּרוּעָ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֔ה וְהַקּ֥וֹל נִשְׁמַ֖ע עַד־לְמֵרָחֽוֹק׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And not the people [were] distinguishing [the] sound of the shout of the joy from [the] sound of [the] weeping of the people, for the people [were] shouting a shout great, and the sound was heard to from afar.

en.L: And the people could not distinguish the sound of the shout of joy from the sound of the weeping of the people, for the people were shouting with a great shout, and the sound was heard far away.
en.B: No one could tell the sound of the shouts of joy from the sound of the people's weeping, because the people were shouting so loudly that the sound was heard far away.
en.R: No one could tell the shouts of joy apart from the sound of crying, because the people were so loud. The noise could be heard far away.

es.L: Y el pueblo no podía distinguir el sonido del grito de alegría del sonido del llanto del pueblo, porque el pueblo gritaba con gran júbilo, y el sonido se oía desde lejos.
es.B: Nadie podía distinguir el sonido de los gritos de alegría del sonido del llanto del pueblo, porque el pueblo gritaba tan fuerte que el sonido se oía desde lejos.
es.R: Nadie podía distinguir los gritos de alegría del sonido del llanto, porque la gente gritaba muy fuerte. El ruido se oía desde muy lejos.

sw.L: Na watu hawakuweza kupambanua sauti ya kelele za furaha na sauti ya kilio cha watu, kwa maana watu walikuwa wakipiga kelele kwa sauti kuu, na sauti ikasikika mbali.
sw.B: Hakuna aliyeweza kutofautisha sauti ya kelele za furaha na sauti ya kilio cha watu, kwa sababu watu walipiga kelele kwa nguvu sana hata sauti ikasikika mbali.
sw.R: Hakuna aliyeweza kutofautisha kelele za furaha na sauti ya kilio, kwa sababu watu walipiga kelele sana. Kelele hizo zilisikika mbali.

decisions.choice: the people could not distinguish: no one could tell the sounds apart
decisions.reason: "The people" here are the hearers, the whole crowd: the joy and the weeping were mixed in one great noise.

decisions.choice: for the people were shouting: the reason the sounds could not be told apart
decisions.reason: The joining word gives the reason: the shout was so great that it covered the weeping, and it carried far beyond the temple site. The chapter closes on the sound of joy and grief together.

decisions.choice: No one could tell
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put "the people could not distinguish" as "no one could tell", since the same people did the shouting and the weeping.
